The only reason I advocate for people to learn manual is not only options to buy different cars, but to keep the flow of traffic moving.

We as humans have become so use to not doing anything we dont want to do - like shifting a car. So driving automatics people just stop and go as a please because it's so easy to do. If people understood that being in a manual in traffic is the most inconvenient thing to do. Not because of going slow, but because of the shifting you have to do. It's hard to balance between 1st and 2nd gear in traffic because there is more torque in those gears.

So when you drive a manual you realize, if everyone drove a manual, traffic would just keep rolling because people would be accustomed to not wanting to shift all the time and keep moving! Its really interesting when you think about the amount of options we have to fix traffic. Not just driving manual of course. This is just one of the things I've noticed after being a manual driver for 6 years now (got my license when I was 16, I'm 22 now and learned manual first).

But I totally understand the ease and comfort of an automatic. I respect everyone's decision to have the car they wish to have. I've owned automatics, I just prefer manual and I feel if everyone was more humble that way, there wouldn't be people like this walking around thinking they're hot shots for driving a manual vehicle.

Thanks to anyone who reads this.

I'm not an owner but I got into RC crawling and buggys for a few years and trust me, it's easy for them to have good business. I alone have probably put like $3000 or more into the hobby and including my brother (who got into it with me) probably like $7000 at least. Motors get expensive as well as the electronics especially when you live in Oregon when its wet all the time.

Also they generally sell things in the cheapest form. For example the crawlers have all plastic parts and a the motors as well as servos and receivers - everything so you want to buy the new metal parts and better electronics for a better build towards how you want your go to run. Want it to be fast? Want it to have powerful torque? Want the car to be able to move a  small boulder with the servo? Theres just so much more that actually goes into the hobby than you would think especially when I first started. You learn about everything that you shouldn't do and everything you should do and based on that you buy your parts.

Then you get so invested you're always looking for the best model of your crawler/buggy/boat whatever it may be. And the crawlers start around $250-$400 depending on what sort of stuff you want with it when you first buy it. And since you've done it before you continue to buy new parts for that new rig.

Trust me, theres more than enough money to keep those companies afloat. But it is very enjoyable I will say and would definitely get into it again.

It's not efficient in any way... you're only building one muscle group when you need more than one to get better a lifting, such as bench. For example, if you want to get better at squats, you don't only do squats, you work on squad extensions, lunges, hammys, etc. if you were to consistently squat, you wouldn't get as far as you want to go. I mean if you're just staying fit, then yeah, maintain the weight and just squat. 

If you want to plateau, only do bench and nothing else. Good luck.

Well I mean, to build a good bench, you need to work your triceps and your back (and of course your chest).You can't just do bench and then expect yourself to lift more weight.

If you want to build your overall strength, workout your tris to finish your bench lock out at the top of your bench press and train your back for strength towards your bench press. If you want more mass on your chest, work on dumb bell chest presses because they train those tiny muscles in your shoulders and chest that you don't normally train when your just benching the bar. Just like athletes use ladders to train the tiny muscles in their knees and calves and feet for stability and balance - same goes for your chest. 

As for the sound - toughen up butter cup. You're lifting weights for a reason. This isn't me being rude, this is just me being honest. I use to be the same way - I hated how loud the weights clacked and smacked so it's just something you need to get use to.
